tier_rationale.T1_wall1_packet: The open Wall 1 ruling. Holds most of the identified evidence bearing on the registered claim; nothing downstream can be settled before these are read.
tier_rationale.T1_primary_identified: Identified designs inside a primary cell. These carry the GRADE rating for their arm.
tier_rationale.T2_primary_relevant: Primary-cell records the screen kept outright. The pooled or narrative core of each arm.
tier_rationale.T3_primary_uncertain: Primary-cell records the screen could not confirm. Their routing is decided at full text, and the CELL BALANCE depends on how they resolve.
tier_rationale.T3_link1_identified: Identified designs on link 1. They cannot carry a fertility verdict but they are the chapter's only leverage on whether the arrangement responds to anything exogenous.
tier_rationale.T4_insufficient_resolve_at_retrieval: Not routable on the visible record. Retrieval IS the screen for these.
tier_rationale.T5_link1: Mechanism evidence for link 1. Retrieve after the primary cells.
tier_rationale.T6_theory_stream: Theory and framing. Read, do not pool.

meta.retrieval_warning: Report retrieval as a CROSS-TAB of tier by outcome, never as one percentage. A 70% rate that misses the identified designs is worse than a 40% rate that gets them.

queue.title: Infrastructure and the American Family: Material Conditions, Household Structure, and the Visibility Gap, 1973–2024
queue.note: No abstract; 'Infrastructure and the American Family: MATERIAL CONDITIONS, HOUSEHOLD STRUCTURE, and the Visibility Gap, 1973-2024'. Names material conditions and household structure together over fifty years; Wall 1 territory. Trace.

queue.title: Housing Careers and Demographic Change: Life Courses, Inequality, and Intergenerational Housing Futures
queue.note: No abstract; 'HOUSING CAREERS AND DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGE: Life Courses, Inequality, and INTERGENERATIONAL HOUSING FUTURES'. Wall 1's framing with the intergenerational dimension named in the title. Trace for the second-read packet.

queue.title: Aging Population and Lower Fertility Affect Housing Market
queue.note: Philippine policy note attributing slowed HOUSEHOLD FORMATION to falling fertility, ageing and LIMITED ACCESS TO AFFORDABLE HOUSING, with extended and multifamily households persisting despite a growing preference for living alone. Wall 1 in a Southeast Asian middle-income setting.

queue.title: Why do young adults coreside with their parents?
queue.note: 'WHY DO YOUNG ADULTS CORESIDE WITH THEIR PARENTS?' in Real Estate Economics: nearly one in two US adults aged 18-29 now lives with parents against one in four in 1960, and a Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition identifies a role for HOUSING AFFORDABILITY against the labour-market and marriage-delay explanations. It decomposes the very trend the pre-launch arm rests on, and it puts Wall 1's variable in competition with the alternatives rather than assuming one. Second-read packet.

queue.title: The trifecta of adulthood: Housing, partnering and childbearing trajectories
queue.note: 'THE TRIFECTA OF ADULTHOOD: HOUSING, PARTNERING AND CHILDBEARING TRAJECTORIES', on the de-standardisation of adulthood pathways in EAST ASIA. All three of Wall 1's elements taken as one trajectory object, in the region where the extended configuration dominates. The best single framing of the chapter's whole problem found in the screen.

queue.title: Households and families
queue.note: HOUSING CAREERS against household and family dynamics, framed through the second demographic transition and a life-course toolbox. Wall 1's chain as a chapter-length treatment.

queue.title: LIVING ARRANGEMENT AND HOMEOWNERSHIP IMPACTS ON FERTILITY INTENTION TO ACHIEVE THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS
queue.venue: Journal of Environmental Science and Sustainable Development
queue.note: THE HAND-ADDED RECORD, now with an abstract. LIVING ARRANGEMENTS and HOMEOWNERSHIP against FERTILITY INTENTION in Indonesia, ordinal logistic regression on national survey data. It carries both Wall 1 variables in one model, and it is one of the two records the boolean query could not reach -- the 226 supplement has now earned itself back twice.

queue.title: The Effect of Financial Resources on Homeownership, Marriage, and Fertility: Evidence from State Lotteries
queue.note: STATE LOTTERY WINS against HOMEOWNERSHIP, MARRIAGE AND FERTILITY for young adults, on the universe of US tax data 2000-2019. As clean an exogenous financial shock as exists, with all three lifecycle outcomes estimated together. The exposure is money rather than the arrangement, so C.3.e owns it -- but it bounds how much of the housing-fertility link is pure liquidity, which the Wall 1 read needs.

queue.title: Childbearing Behavior in the Light of Different Housing Regimes: First Births in Sweden 1975-2004
queue.note: 'Childbearing Behavior in the Light of Different HOUSING REGIMES: FIRST BIRTHS in Sweden 1975-2004', opening on the premise that affordable housing is directly linked to young people's ability to FORM INDEPENDENT HOUSEHOLDS and in turn to childbearing. Thirty years of Swedish first births against housing regime -- Wall 1's chain with register-grade data. Second-read packet.

queue.title: ЖИЛИЩНЫЕ УСЛОВИЯ И ДЕТНОСТЬ: СВЯЗЬ И ВОЗМОЖНОСТИ ВЛИЯНИЯ
queue.note: Russian-language conference paper stating the chain directly: housing availability influences the decision to LEAVE THE PARENTAL HOME and start one's own family, and housing provision relates to birth rates. Wall 1's mechanism in a Russian setting.

queue.title: Housing as a Fertility Trap: The Inability of States, Markets, or Families to Provide Adequate Housing in East Central Europe
queue.venue: East European Politics and Societies and Cultures
queue.note: 'HOUSING AS A FERTILITY TRAP' -- housing finance and policy in East Central Europe explicitly to understand the connection between housing, INDEPENDENT HOUSEHOLD FORMATION, and demographic outcomes. Wall 1's mechanism named as the title of the paper, in a region the frame is thin on. Second-read packet.

queue.title: Subsidized Housing and the Transition to Adulthood
queue.note: 'SUBSIDIZED HOUSING AND THE TRANSITION TO ADULTHOOD' in Demography: the effect of the US federal subsidised-housing programme on HOW AND WHEN children become adults. Scope §4 design 3 -- administrative allocation of dwellings -- realised in a peer-reviewed demography journal, in the arm that has almost no identified evidence. Priority read.

queue.title: Waking Up from the American Dream: On the Experience of Young Americans during the Housing Boom of the 2000s
queue.venue: Journal of money credit and banking
queue.note: IDENTIFIED, AND THE BEST WALL-1 RECORD YET. Exploits regional US house-price variation in the 2000s boom against young Americans' HOME OWNERSHIP, HOUSEHOLD FORMATION and FERTILITY, with a NOVEL INSTRUMENT built on predetermined industrial structure. All three outcomes in one instrumented design -- it can decompose how much of the price effect on fertility runs through household formation, which is exactly the non-additivity question §2 inherited from C.2.c and could not answer. Priority read; second-read packet.

queue.title: Housing Multigenerational Households in Australian Cities: Evidence from Sydney and Brisbane at the Turn of the 21st century
queue.note: HOUSING multigenerational households in Sydney and Brisbane. The dwelling stock as the constraint on the arrangement -- Wall 1 from the built-environment side.

queue.title: Delayed and depressed: from expensive housing to smaller families
queue.note: 'Delayed and depressed: from expensive housing to smaller families' -- a framework in which housing acts on LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, partnering and having children, all of which extend later in life. Wall 1's mechanism stated as a framework; belongs in the second-read packet.

queue.title: The Impact of Housing Welfare System on Family Formation and Family Dissolution in Qatar
queue.venue: Qatar Foundation Annual Research Conference Proceedings Volume 2016 Issue 1
queue.note: Qatar's HOUSING WELFARE SYSTEM against family formation and dissolution. A policy that allocates housing to families -- design 3's shape in a setting the frame lacks entirely.

queue.title: A study on the characteristic of Household Living Arrangements in Taipei Metropolitan Area
queue.note: Taipei household transitions in the PSFD panel, with one of the modelled groups being households MOVING FROM LIVING WITH PARENTS TO RENTING. Prices, commuting cost and the arrangement in one multinomial logit -- the same Taiwanese panel as the housing-options record in batch 17.

queue.title: Do housing options affect child birth decisions? Evidence from Taiwan
queue.note: 'Do housing options affect child birth decisions?' Taiwan PSFD panel, with the option set spanning RENTING, OWNING, LIVING WITH PARENTS OR SIBLINGS, living in a house bought by parents, and staff housing, against fertility decisions. Tenure and the arrangement in ONE choice set with a birth outcome -- the single best record for adjudicating Wall 1 empirically rather than by ruling. Priority read for the second-read packet.

queue.title: Fostering Household Formation: Evidence from a Spanish Rental Subsidy
queue.venue: The B E Journal of Economic Analysis & Policy
queue.note: PUBLISHED VERSION of Aparicio-Fenoll and Oppedisano. Spain's 2008 monthly cash subsidy conditional on renting, DiD on the ELIGIBILITY AGE THRESHOLD, with living apart from parents, living with a partner AND CHILDBEARING as outcomes, larger for lower earners and in high-rent areas. The chapter's single identified pre-launch design; keep this over the SSRN preprints in batches 12 and 14.

queue.title: The Marginal Cost of a Bedroom: An Australian Case Study
queue.note: THE MARGINAL COST OF A BEDROOM in Australia, against rising multigenerational and group living and policy incentives aimed at fertility. Prices the space constraint that C.2.c owns while the arrangement is the changing quantity -- Wall 1 from the housing-economics side.

queue.title: Family dynamics and housing
queue.note: 'Family dynamics and housing': a reflection connecting LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, marriage, parenthood and separation to housing, with the limitations discussed. This is Wall 1 written from the demography side; it belongs in the second-read packet alongside the JEEA and Spanish-subsidy records.

queue.title: Fostering the Emancipation of Young People: Evidence from a Spanish Rental Subsidy
queue.note: No abstract on this record, but it is the SSRN preprint of Aparicio-Fenoll and Oppedisano's Spanish rental subsidy study -- the chapter's single identified pre-launch design, DiD on the eligibility-age threshold with living apart from parents, partnering AND childbearing as outcomes. Duplicate of the BE JEAP version in batch 15; keep the published one.

queue.title: The Dynamics of Participation in Subsidized Housing Programs in the U.S.
queue.note: Participation dynamics in US SUBSIDISED HOUSING programmes. A housing-programme exposure aimed at where poor households live; Wall 1's mixed territory, and a possible design-3 source of variation if allocation is rationed.

queue.title: Does High Cost of Mortgage Debt Explain Why Young Adults Live with Their Parents?
queue.venue: Journal of the European Economic Association
queue.note: JEEA published version of the mortgage-cost paper seen as an SSRN preprint in batch 9. Estimates the impact of the COST OF A MORTGAGE on the probability of leaving the parental home, explicitly motivated by the implications for FERTILITY, and explains the North-South European gradient the pre-launch arm rests on. Wall 1's mixed case with an identified design: the treatment is a price, the target is the arrangement. Priority read, and it belongs in the Wall 1 second-read packet with Aparicio-Fenoll. Duplicate pair with W1529588091 -- keep this published version.

queue.title: Polítiques d'habitatge social i de joves
queue.note: Catalan article on SOCIAL HOUSING POLICY FOR YOUNG PEOPLE and their difficulties accessing housing. A policy aimed at the arrangement through price -- Wall 1's mixed case, in the Spanish setting where the Aparicio-Fenoll subsidy was evaluated.

queue.title: Does Limited Access to Mortgage Debt Explain Why Young Adults Live with Their Parents?
queue.note: No abstract, but the title is decisive and it sits exactly on Wall 1: 'Does Limited Access to Mortgage Debt Explain Why Young Adults Live with Their Parents?' Credit access as the driver of pre-launch co-residence -- C.3.e's variation producing A.23's arrangement. Full-text read, and it belongs in the Wall 1 second-read packet.

queue.title: The impact of household structure on fertility: A study in Vietnam
queue.note: 'THE IMPACT OF HOUSEHOLD STRUCTURE ON FERTILITY: A STUDY IN VIETNAM' in Demographic Research: nine years of panel data on 1,200 households with a FIXED EFFECTS model to control unobserved household factors. Panel fixed effects on this chapter's exact estimand -- the cleanest observational identification strategy in either arm, because it differences out the time-invariant selection into co-residence that §3 warns about. Priority read.

queue.title: Extended Family Structures Exert a causal Influence on Fertility
queue.note: 'EXTENDED FAMILY STRUCTURES EXERT A CAUSAL INFLUENCE ON FERTILITY' -- and it names the gap this chapter's extended arm sits in: the alloparenting literature concentrates on the mother's parents and parents-in-law, while the fertility impact of EXTENDED FAMILY STRUCTURE itself has had much less attention. A causal claim on exactly the registered estimand. Priority read and priority scrutiny.

queue.title: Intergenerational living arrangements and marital fertility in Japan: a counterfactual approach
queue.note: THE EXTENDED ARM'S SECOND IDENTIFIED RECORD, and it names the problem explicitly: 'INTERGENERATIONAL LIVING ARRANGEMENTS AND MARITAL FERTILITY IN JAPAN: A COUNTERFACTUAL APPROACH', investigating CAUSAL links using the 2010 and 2015 Japanese National Fertility Surveys, and reporting that co-residence with the husband's parents is positively associated with completed marital fertility in the unadjusted comparison. A counterfactual framework applied to exactly this chapter's estimand. Priority read -- with the Taiwanese endogenous-coresidence paper it forms the extended arm's identified core.

queue.title: AN EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF MARITAL STATUS IN JAPAN
queue.note: FIXED-EFFECT 2SLS on Japanese prefectural data linking marital status, the fertility rate and socioeconomic factors, reporting that the MALE CO-RESIDENCE RATE has a positive effect. A pre-launch arrangement variable inside an instrumented aggregate model -- rare in this arm, though the unit is the prefecture rather than the person. Priority read for the identification strategy.

queue.title: Geology, Household Formation Rules and the Demand for Sons in Vietnam
queue.note: No abstract, but the title is remarkable and squarely on §4's enumeration: 'GEOLOGY, HOUSEHOLD FORMATION RULES and the Demand for Sons in Vietnam'. Geology as a plausibly exogenous determinant of household formation rules is a design the scope never imagined. Priority trace -- if it delivers, it is the only geographic instrument for the arrangement in the frame.

queue.title: Coresidence With Husband’s Parents, Labor Supply, and Duration to First Birth
queue.note: THE EXTENDED ARM'S BEST RECORD. Duration to FIRST BIRTH among Taiwanese married women born 1933-68, treating CO-RESIDENCE WITH THE HUSBAND'S PARENTS and labour supply as ENDOGENOUS, with a full-information maximum-likelihood duration model with endogenous binary variables. It confronts §3's anticipation problem directly rather than controlling for it, and it separates the labour-supply channel the scope named as the largest route-out. Priority read.

queue.title: “Family-Anchored” transitions to adult life in Mexico
queue.note: 'FAMILY-ANCHORED' TRANSITIONS TO ADULT LIFE IN MEXICO: young adults commonly CO-RESIDE WITH OWN PARENTS OR OTHER EXTENDED FAMILY WHEN FORMING A FIRST PARTNERSHIP OR BECOMING A PARENT, and the authors say the practice has scarcely been studied. That is a configuration neither §6 value covers -- the birth happens INSIDE the parental household rather than after leaving it -- and it dissolves the assumed ordering that §3 is built on. Priority read; likely a scope amendment.

queue.title: Family migration in Chinese superstar cities: are fertility intentions of migrants affected by co-resident parents?
queue.note: 'Family migration in Chinese superstar cities: are FERTILITY INTENTIONS of migrants affected by CO-RESIDENT PARENTS?' The exposure is co-residence, the outcome is fertility intention, and the migrant setting partly breaks the usual selection into co-residence because the parents move to the city.

queue.title: Impact of Close Residence between Aging Parents and Adult Daughters on Grandchild Care and First Births
queue.note: THE PROXIMITY CELL'S THIRD RECORD AND ITS BEST DESIGN. Close residence between aging parents and adult daughters against grandchild care and FIRST BIRTHS in Korean KLoSA panel data, using an explicit TWO-STAGE approach BECAUSE grandchild care can only occur after childbirth. That is §3's ordering problem recognised and built into the estimator rather than assumed away. Priority read.

queue.title: Family forms and reproductive behaviour: A comparative study of nuclear and extended households in Morogoro region
queue.venue: International Journal of Geography Geology and Environment
queue.note: 'FAMILY FORMS AND REPRODUCTIVE BEHAVIOUR: a comparative study of NUCLEAR AND EXTENDED HOUSEHOLDS' in Morogoro, Tanzania -- and it states the confounding problem itself, that education and income may explain the apparent extended-household fertility premium. Sub-Saharan setting; the extended arm has almost nothing there.

queue.title: Mapping Early Mid-Life Trajectories and Ultimate Childlessness: A Multichannel Sequence Analysis in Finland and Belgium
queue.note: MULTICHANNEL SEQUENCE ANALYSIS of early mid-life trajectories against ULTIMATE CHILDLESSNESS in Finland and Belgium, with delays in RESIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE among the channels. The sequence method §3 wants, carried through to a completed-fertility endpoint rather than a timing one. Priority read.

queue.title: Transitions to Motherhood in a Low-Fertility Country: Timing, Type, and Order of Life Course Events
queue.note: Transitions to motherhood in SPAIN: first union, LEAVING HOME, economic independence and employment against the PROBABILITY OF MOTHERHOOD, with attention to timing and order. The registered setting, the registered mechanism, and both links estimated together. Priority read.

queue.title: Dynamic interplay of kinship and net-fertility: a comprehensive analysis across demographic transitions in Mexico
queue.note: GRANDPARENTAL CO-RESIDENCE against NET FERTILITY in MEXICO at three points spanning the whole demographic transition -- 1930 pre-transitional, 1970 growth, 2015 decline -- on census microdata with Poisson and multinomial models. The only record in the frame that estimates this chapter's estimand across PM, FDT and SDT conditions in one country, which bears directly on whether the arrangement's effect is regime-dependent. Priority read.

queue.title: Grandparents “on board”: How they translate into the households’ fertility decisions
queue.note: Published version of the batch-1 record: whether CO-RESIDENCE OF OLDER PARENTS with adult children of reproductive age raises the chance of a MULTICHILD FAMILY, Luxembourg Wealth Study, 11 European countries. Finds NO support -- a directly-on-cell null in the extended arm, and a European counterweight to the positive East Asian estimates.

queue.title: CORESIDING WITH PARENTS, SON PREFERENCE, AND WOMEN’S DESIRE FOR ADDITIONAL CHILDREN IN VIETNAM
queue.note: 'CORESIDING WITH PARENTS, son preference, and WOMEN'S DESIRE FOR ADDITIONAL CHILDREN IN VIETNAM' -- co-residence in the exposure and a fertility-desire outcome, with the in-laws' pressure for a male heir as the stated mechanism, set against declining multigenerational households under urbanisation. Directly on the extended arm's estimand.

queue.title: Post-marital residence patterns and the timing of reproduction: evidence from a matrilineal society
queue.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
queue.note: 'POST-MARITAL RESIDENCE PATTERNS AND THE TIMING OF REPRODUCTION' in a MATRILINEAL Tibetan population, and it states the chapter's own conditionality: the relationship depends on whether CO-RESIDENT KIN ARE COOPERATORS OR COMPETITORS. That is §5's two-sign problem, derived from theory rather than observed as a nuisance. Priority read.

queue.title: Spatial Bayesian modeling of household structure and fertility in municipalities of Mexico
queue.note: Spatial Bayesian modelling of HOUSEHOLD COMPOSITION against municipal FERTILITY levels across MEXICO in 2020. An ecological design, so it inherits the inference problem, but it is an arrangement-to-fertility estimate at sub-national resolution in a Latin American setting the frame otherwise lacks.

queue.title: The Influence of Kin Proximity on the Reproductive Success of American Couples, 1900–1910
queue.note: 'The Influence of KIN PROXIMITY on the REPRODUCTIVE SUCCESS of American Couples, 1900-1910' in Demography: kin availability against couples' birth spacing and child survival, using full-count historical census data. Only the second record in the proximity cell, and by far the largest -- and it separates spacing from survival, which the extended arm's evolutionary literature usually conflates.

queue.title: Moving out the parental home and partnership formation as social determinants of low fertility
queue.note: Gated anchor, in its Vienna Yearbook debate form: 'MOVING OUT THE PARENTAL HOME AND PARTNERSHIP FORMATION AS SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF LOW FERTILITY'. The registered hypothesis stated as a position in a field debate; the other contributions to the same debate are separate records in this batch and route out.

queue.title: Curse of the Mummy‐ji : The Influence of Mothers‐in‐Law on Women in India †
queue.note: Published AJAE version of 'Curse of the Mummy-ji': mothers-in-law constraining young married women's networks, mobility and reproductive health in patrilocal India. Keep this over the RePEc preprint in batch 21.

queue.title: “We’re Fine at Home”: Young People, Family and Low Fertility in Spain
queue.note: "'We're Fine at Home': Young People, Family and Low Fertility in SPAIN" -- fieldwork on how young Spaniards understand their own role in the birth-rate decline. Qualitative, and the title states the mechanism §1 hypothesises from the inside: staying is comfortable, not merely constrained.

queue.title: The transition to adulthood in China, Germany and the US: Prevalence and timing in private and professional life
queue.note: Timing of LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, first marriage and FIRST PARENTHOOD compared across CHINA, GERMANY and the USA for cohorts born 1933-1988, using large panel studies. All three events, three countries spanning both arms' regimes, and cohort depth -- the best comparative record in the frame for placing the two configurations side by side.

queue.title: Becoming Independent: Leaving Home, Cohabitation, Marriage, and Parenthood
queue.note: 'Becoming Independent: LEAVING HOME, Cohabitation, Marriage, and PARENTHOOD' -- the chapter takes the whole chain as its subject and notes that young adults increasingly live independently BEFORE marriage, which decouples the arrangement from the union. That decoupling is what makes A.23 separable from A.7 at all.

queue.title: Curse of the Mummy-ji: The Influence of Mothers-in-Law on Women's Social Networks, Mobility, and Reproductive Health in India
queue.note: 'Curse of the Mummy-ji': how MOTHERS-IN-LAW constrain young married women's social networks, mobility and REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH in patrilocal rural India, framed explicitly as intergenerational power dynamics WITHIN THE HOUSEHOLD. The extended arm's mechanism at its most direct, with network data.

queue.title: Independencia Residencial, Dedicación Laboral Y Fertilidad De Los Jóvenes Españoles. Un Análisis Por Comunidades Autónomas
queue.note: Companion to the preceding record and the stronger of the pair: RESIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE, labour attachment AND FERTILITY of Spanish youth by autonomous community. Leaving the parental home and having children in one regional analysis, in the setting the registered claim is about. Priority read; likely duplicate pair with W3011464401 -- resolve at assembly.

queue.title: Independencia residencial y dedicación laboral de los jóvenes españoles: Un análisis por Comunidades Autónomas
queue.note: RESIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE and labour attachment of Spanish youth analysed BY AUTONOMOUS COMMUNITY. Within-country regional variation in the registered setting -- exactly what Wall 3 asks for and what the cross-national backbone records cannot supply.

queue.title: Household precariousness and youth living arrangements in Spain: evidence for a complete business cycle
queue.note: HOUSEHOLD PRECARIOUSNESS and youth LIVING ARRANGEMENTS in SPAIN across a complete business cycle, with the stated consequence that economic difficulty delays EMANCIPATION AND CHILDBEARING. The registered setting, both links, and a full cycle rather than a single recession -- which is closer to a repeated natural experiment than most of the arm.

queue.title: Effects of the Conversation and Support of Family Network Factors on Fertility Intentions among Korean Married Women
queue.venue: The Korean Journal of Community Living Science
queue.note: Conversation with and support from PARENTS AND PARENTS-IN-LAW, separately from husband and siblings, against FERTILITY INTENTIONS of Korean married women with at least one child. Panel data, and it separates the natal from the affinal side -- the distinction §6's configuration split needs and most records collapse.

queue.title: The timing of marriage vis-à-vis coresidence and childbearing in Europe and the United States
queue.note: Links the TIMING OF MARRIAGE to CORESIDENCE and CHILDBEARING across European countries and the US, extending Holland's marriage typology. All three events in one framework, cross-nationally -- descriptive, but it is the map of the sequence the chapter has to explain.

queue.title: Home-leaving and Parenthood : Timing of home-leaving and the relation to childbearing behavior in Sweden
queue.venue: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
queue.note: 'Home-leaving and Parenthood': the TIMING OF LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME against the timing of first birth in Sweden, asking whether leaving at a younger or older age RELATIVE TO THE PREVAILING NORM predicts childbearing. The relative-to-norm construction is a partial answer to §3 -- it compares people against their cohort's schedule rather than against each other's realised sequence. Priority read.

queue.title: Race, Family Status, and Young Women’s Residential and Financial Dependency: 1970 to 2010
queue.note: Whether rising INTERGENERATIONAL CO-RESIDENCE and financial dependency among young Black and White women are associated with declining marriage and rising NONMARITAL PARENTHOOD, US Census and ACS 1970-2010. Forty years of the exposure and a fertility outcome in one series, with a race split -- and it explicitly entertains the reverse arrow, that parenthood drives the co-residence.

queue.title: Do parents matter? Intergenerational ties and fertility preferences in a low-fertility context
queue.note: 'Do parents matter?' Multidimensional INTERGENERATIONAL TIES against married women's intended and ideal family size in Jiangsu, an extremely low-fertility Chinese province. Directly on the extended arm's estimand, with the parents' own preferences among the measured dimensions -- which is the mechanism the mother-in-law records describe qualitatively.

queue.title: Parenthood and Leaving Home in Young Adulthood
queue.note: No abstract, but 'Parenthood and Leaving Home in Young Adulthood' in Population Research and Policy Review names both links and the pre-launch population. Direction of the arrow is not visible from the title and matters -- trace.

queue.title: Effects of Ethnic Composition and Living with In-laws on Fertility of Foreign Wives in Korea: An Analysis of Neighborhood Effects
queue.note: No abstract, but the title is decisive on both axes: effects of ethnic composition and LIVING WITH IN-LAWS on the FERTILITY of foreign wives in Korea, with neighbourhood effects. A direct extended-arm estimate; trace for the design.

queue.title: The Problematic Transition to Adulthood in Italy. A Comparison Before and After the Beginning of the Global Crisis
queue.note: LEAVING THE FAMILY OF ORIGIN and ENTERING PARENTHOOD taken as the two critical steps, in ITALY, compared before and after the global crisis. The registered hypothesis's setting with both links in one survey and a macro shock splitting the sample -- the closest the pre-launch arm has to a natural comparison.

queue.title: FP-13-01 Coresident vs. Non-Coresident Young Adults, 2011
queue.note: American Community Survey profile comparing CORESIDING with NON-CORESIDING young adults on enrolment, employment, wages, PARENTHOOD and marriage. Exactly the contrast the registered claim implies -- and exactly the contrast §3 says is uninterpretable, since it conditions on having launched. Valuable as the descriptive benchmark and as the clearest instance of the chapter's central identification problem.

queue.title: Starting a Family at Your Parents’ House: Multigenerational Households and Below Replacement Fertility in Urban Bulgaria
queue.note: Full-title version of the gated anchor: multigenerational households and below-replacement fertility in URBAN BULGARIA, contrasting Italy's postponement with Bulgaria's early childbearing under the same strong multigenerational links. The contrast is the chapter's own configuration problem stated as a finding -- the same arrangement produces opposite timing in two settings.

queue.title: Household formation rules, fertility and female labour supply: Evidence from post-communist countries
queue.note: No abstract, but the title is decisive on both axes: HOUSEHOLD FORMATION RULES against FERTILITY and female labour supply across post-communist countries. Journal of Comparative Economics. The design is invisible here; priority trace, and the labour-supply co-outcome lets it test the OFF_OUTCOME_LABOUR_SUPPLY boundary.

queue.title: Fertility intentions depend on intergenerational relations: A life course perspective
queue.note: Fertility INTENTIONS against current intergenerational family relationships and childhood parental divorce, opening by noting that the influence of the parental home on fertility is well established but the MECHANISM is unclear. That is the chapter's own question, asked directly, with a pre-determined childhood exposure. Priority read.

queue.title: Family Structure, Marital Fertility and Premarital Sex among Married and Never-Married Women in Contemporary China
queue.note: PATRILOCAL RESIDENCE against MARITAL FERTILITY in contemporary China, testing the traditional link between residence and early high fertility against a period of rapid decline. A direct arrangement-to-fertility estimate in the extended arm's largest setting.

queue.title: INTERGENERATIONAL PROXIMITY AND THE FERTILITY INTENTIONS OF MARRIED WOMEN
queue.note: Gated anchor. Nationally representative surveys of married women in JAPAN AND ITALY, arguing that explanations of very low fertility in strong-family countries emphasise childrearing costs and ignore the offsetting influence of DISTINCTIVE LIVING ARRANGEMENTS. The proximity cell's core record, and it spans the two settings the two arms live in.

queue.title: Husbands, Wives, and In-Laws: Family Dynamics and Childbearing Behavior in Nepal.
queue.note: Relationship dynamics between wives and their HUSBANDS' FAMILIES and their interconnection with childbearing behaviour in rural Nepal, explicitly against the thin empirical base on extended-family systems. Directly on the extended arm's estimand.

queue.title: Influence of mothers-in-law on young couples’ family planning decisions in rural India
queue.note: Influence of MOTHERS-IN-LAW on young couples' family planning decisions in rural India, in patrilocal households, examining how intra-family relations shape contraceptive method and timing. The extended arm's mechanism at the decision level.

queue.title: Ties That Matter: Cultural Norms and Family Formation in Western Europe
queue.note: Giuliano's cultural-norms and family-formation chapter: in Italy, Portugal, Greece and Spain 70-80% of 18-33 year olds live at home, alongside rising age at marriage and declining fertility. The registered hypothesis's central stylised fact with a cultural-transmission mechanism attached. Priority read -- Giuliano's identification strategy elsewhere uses second-generation immigrants, which is a route to within-setting variation that scope §4 did not enumerate.

queue.title: The Timing of Leaving the Parental Home and Its Linkages to Other Life Course Events in Turkey
queue.note: Turkish DHS: timing of leaving the parental home against labour force entry, family formation AND FIRST BIRTH, split into early, on-time and late home-leavers. Arrangement timing as exposure with a birth outcome. NOTE: same title as the Marriage & Family Review record already gated as an anchor -- likely a duplicate pair to resolve at assembly.

queue.title: Parental Homes as Feathered Nets: Home-Leaving Trajectories of Young People in China
queue.venue: Socius Sociological Research for a Dynamic World
queue.note: 'PARENTAL HOMES AS FEATHERED NETS: HOME-LEAVING TRAJECTORIES OF YOUNG PEOPLE IN CHINA' in Socius, arguing the STAY/LEAVE DICHOTOMY is inadequate for prolonged, REVERSIBLE and complex transitions, especially in East Asia where intergenerational co-residence is a long-standing norm. This is §9's measurement problem stated as the paper's premise, in the setting where both configurations coexist. Priority read.

queue.title: Short- and long-distance home-leaving and home-returning: exploring the role of life course transitions
queue.note: SHORT- AND LONG-DISTANCE HOME-LEAVING AND HOME-RETURNING and their links to other life-course transitions, opening on the observation that co-residence with parents is one of the commonest young-adult arrangements and that many return after living independently. Distance and reversibility together -- the two measurement dimensions §9 is weakest on.

queue.title: Ideations and Intentions in the Transition to Adulthood: A Cross-European Comparison
queue.note: Cross-European comparison of IDEATIONS AND INTENTIONS about the timing of EXIT FROM THE PARENTAL HOME, cohabitation, marriage and parenthood. Intentions about the arrangement itself, which no other record measures directly.

queue.title: Youth Transition Pathways in Norway: How Education, Work and Gender Matter
queue.venue: Perspectives on children and young people
queue.note: No abstract; youth transition pathways in Norway. One of four country chapters in the same comparative volume.

queue.title: Youth Transitions in Switzerland: The Relevance of Gendered Life Courses in the Early Twenty-First Century
queue.venue: Perspectives on children and young people
queue.note: Swiss youth transitions covering school-to-work, HOUSING (LEAVING HOME) and domestic transitions including PARENTHOOD, with gendered life courses. The one chapter of the four whose abstract confirms both links are in scope.

queue.title: Young Adults Transitions to Adulthood in the United Kingdom: Protracted Yet Highly Diversified Pathways
queue.venue: Perspectives on children and young people
queue.note: No abstract; protracted and diversified transition pathways in the UK. Same volume.

queue.title: Life-Course Patterns of Young Russian-Origin Estonians: An Origin-Destination Comparison
queue.note: Origin-destination comparison of life-course statuses in the transition to adulthood among young Russian-origin Estonians. A migrant-origin comparison of the transition schedule -- close to the second-generation identification strategy Giuliano uses.

queue.title: Uncertain Futures Among Those in Precarious Employment in Japan
queue.venue: Perspectives on children and young people
queue.note: No abstract; precarious employment and uncertain futures in Japan. Fifth country chapter of the youth-transitions volume.

queue.title: The Way We Move: The Role of Parents in Geographical Mobility
queue.note: The role of PARENTS in their children's GEOGRAPHICAL MOBILITY in childhood and adulthood. Parental influence on the move itself, which is the decision link 1 models.

queue.title: Prolonged Transitions into Adulthood in Germany
queue.venue: Perspectives on children and young people
queue.note: No abstract; prolonged transitions into adulthood in Germany. Same volume.

queue.title: The transition to adulthood in Europe at the intersection of gender and parental socioeconomic status
queue.note: Transition to adulthood across Europe at the intersection of GENDER and PARENTAL SES, evaluating the timing and risk of HOME-LEAVING among the events. Stratification of link 1 with comparative data.

queue.title: Education systems as life course policies? The example of subnational educational regimes and young adults’ family transitions
queue.note: SUBNATIONAL EDUCATIONAL REGIMES against three transitions -- LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, starting to cohabit, and BECOMING A PARENT. Within-country institutional variation acting on the whole chain, which is what Wall 3 asks for; policy regime rather than the arrangement is the exposure.

queue.title: Five decades of household change across Asian societies
queue.note: FIVE DECADES of household change across ASIAN societies using the newly released CORESIDENCE database. The largest harmonised exposure series available to the extended arm, and a named data resource this chapter should use directly.

queue.title: Living apart together in contemporary Spain: Diverse motivations across life stages
queue.note: No abstract; LIVING APART TOGETHER in contemporary SPAIN and its motivations across life stages. The LAT configuration in the registered setting.

queue.title: Gender imbalance, wife’s bargain power and shrinking household size in Rural China
queue.note: GENDER IMBALANCE and wives' bargaining power against SHRINKING HOUSEHOLD SIZE in rural China. A.10's driver producing this chapter's arrangement.

queue.title: Data Note: Social role transitions (further/higher education, employment, living situation, parenthood, and being a carer) in the G1s of the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC)
queue.note: ALSPAC data note deriving social role transitions including LIVING SITUATION and parenthood by an algorithmic approach. A cohort resource with the arrangement and the birth on one timeline.

queue.title: Pathways to Adulthood in Rural America: A Latent Profile and Latent Transition Analysis of Adult Social Roles
queue.note: No abstract; latent profile and transition analysis of adult social roles in RURAL AMERICA. Companion to the Appalachian record.

queue.title: Transition to Adulthood and the Intergenerational Transmission of Disadvantages Among Young Adults in Spain
queue.note: DELAYED TRANSITION TO ADULTHOOD in SPAIN and the intergenerational transmission of disadvantage, using an intersectional quantitative framework. The registered setting, with inequality as the organising variable rather than culture.

queue.title: 2 Transformation of the Family Structure in Southeast Asia: Trends and Implications
queue.note: Transformation of family structure in SOUTHEAST ASIA under fertility decline, migration and longer lives. Regional exposure trend; the reverse arrow is in the framing.

queue.title: Long goodbyes: pathways of leaving home by gender and destination in Spain
queue.note: 'Long goodbyes': pathways of LEAVING HOME in SPAIN, separating moving out TO LIVE WITH A PARTNER from moving out WITHOUT one. That separation is what makes the arrangement analytically distinct from union formation -- the single most useful distinction for keeping A.23 apart from A.7, in the registered setting.

queue.title: Three‐Generation Households in a Central and Eastern European Country: The Case of Hungary
queue.note: THREE-GENERATION living arrangements in HUNGARY from censuses 1980-2016, with determinants. Central and Eastern Europe, and the 1990-2001 interruption in the decline is a natural discontinuity worth reading about.

queue.title: Coming of Age in Appalachia, Emerging or Expedited Adulthood?
queue.venue: RSF The Russell Sage Foundation Journal of the Social Sciences
queue.note: Transition to adulthood in poor rural Appalachia under persistent poverty and the opioid crisis, with strong family and work norms. An EXPEDITED rather than delayed transition -- the mirror case, and a useful contrast to the Southern European pattern.

queue.title: Continuity and Change in U.S. Children's Family Composition, 1968–2017
queue.note: Fifty years of US children's household composition in the PSID, including the FREQUENCY OF FAMILY MEMBERS' ENTRANCES AND DEPARTURES. Turnover rather than stock -- a measurement §9 should adopt, since co-residence is not an absorbing state.

queue.title: Interactions between educational lifecycle and transition to adulthood: A proposal for a new questionnaire
queue.note: No abstract; a proposed questionnaire on the educational lifecycle and the transition to adulthood. Instrument design rather than evidence.

queue.title: Migration Aspirations and Adolescents’ Ideal age at Union Formation in Western Mexico
queue.note: Migration aspirations and ideal age at union formation in western Mexico, with HOUSEHOLD FORMATION named among the sequenced behaviours migration systems shape. Migration as a route out of the parental home in a Latin American setting.

queue.title: Leaving Parental Home in Selected Central European Countries
queue.note: LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME in the Czech Republic, Poland and the former GDR for women born 1952-1982. Post-socialist cohorts spanning the transition -- a setting where the arrangement changed sharply for reasons outside the individual.

queue.title: Microsimulation of Household and Marital Transitions Leading to Childlessness Among Dutch Women Born Between 1971 and 2000
queue.note: Microsimulation of HOUSEHOLD AND MARITAL TRANSITIONS leading to CHILDLESSNESS among Dutch women born 1971-2000, motivated by transitions to adulthood becoming late, protracted and complex. The full chain modelled to a fertility endpoint; simulation rather than estimation.

queue.title: The Economics of Households in South Africa
queue.note: HOUSEHOLD FORMATION in SOUTH AFRICA, its disruption under apartheid and its changes since, using national micro-data 1995-2018. A setting where household formation was directly constrained by law -- a design-6 candidate the scope did not enumerate.

queue.title: Adaptations to the One-Child Policy: Chinese Young Adults’ Attitudes Toward Elder Care and Living Arrangement After Marriage
queue.note: One-child-generation Chinese young adults' attitudes to elder care and to LIVING ARRANGEMENT AFTER MARRIAGE. Intentions about the extended configuration in the cohort now forming it.

queue.title: Complexity in Employment and Coresidential Trajectories Among (Dis)Advantaged Social Groups in Chile
queue.note: Complexity in employment and CORESIDENTIAL trajectories by social group in CHILE. Sequence complexity as the outcome, in a Latin American setting; pairs with the Chilean subfamilies record in batch 19.

queue.title: Becoming an adult in the new millennium
queue.note: Two Italian studies a decade apart on the transition to adulthood. Repeated cross-sections in the registered setting; the 2003/2013 gap spans the crisis.

queue.title: ‘In a way, you’d like to move with them’: young people, moving away from home, and the roles of parents
queue.note: Parents' role when young people MOVE AWAY FROM HOME, noting that moves have grown more TEMPORARY AND REVERSIBLE. The reversibility point matters for §9: leaving home is not an absorbing state.

queue.title: From Living Apart to Living Together: Do Children Born before the Current Partnership Matter?
queue.note: Transition from LIVING APART TOGETHER to CO-RESIDING, and whether pre-partnership children affect it. The LAT configuration studied as a transition rather than a state -- the fullest treatment of it in the frame.

queue.title: Living arrangements across households in Europe
queue.note: Living arrangements across 21 EUROPEAN countries from the EU Labour Force Survey, by age and sex, 2006 to 2016, with REGIONAL variation. Harmonised exposure measurement with sub-national resolution -- the denominator the pre-launch arm's descriptive claims need.

queue.title: Family and Demographic Issues in Japan
queue.note: Japanese marriage and family change, with marriage and childbirth still tightly coupled. Context for why the pre-launch and extended configurations are hard to separate in Japan.

queue.title: Committed to independence? An exploratory study of living-apart-together (LAT) in contemporary Sweden
queue.note: LIVING-APART-TOGETHER beyond the late twenties in SWEDEN, from the Swedish GGS. The LAT configuration measured in a high-single-household country; relevant to whether partnering and co-residence can be separated.

queue.title: Intergenerational Relationships between Married Children and Their Parents in 21st Century Japan
queue.note: Married children and their parents in 21st-century Japan, tracing the patrilineal rule under which PARENTS LIVE WITH THE HEIR AND HIS FAMILY from the civil code to the present. The institutional history of the extended configuration in its key setting.

queue.title: Changes and Trends in Family Structure in Taiwan, 1990 to 2010
queue.note: Family structure change in TAIWAN 1990-2010 driven by falling fertility and postponed marriage. Exposure trend, with the reverse arrow in the framing.

queue.title: The diversity of union and fertility trajectories in the uk
queue.venue: LA Referencia (Red Federada de Repositorios Institucionales de Publicaciones Científicas)
queue.note: Parents' socioeconomic position against children's transition to FIRST UNION AND PARENTHOOD, UK Household Longitudinal Study, n=35,880. Large panel with both downstream links; the arrangement is not the exposure but the data would support it.

queue.title: What makes someone adult? The role of family transitions and independence in opinions about becoming adult
queue.note: What criteria Hungarians consider necessary for adulthood, with INDEPENDENCE and family transitions among them, ESS. The subjective adult-status mechanism §1 names, measured as an attitude.

queue.title: Economic difficulties during the transition into adulthood in Finland : a register-based study
queue.note: REGISTER-based study of economic difficulties during the transition to adulthood in Finland. Register measurement of the transition; C.5.a owns the exposure.

queue.title: Essays on Family Dynamics : Partnering, Fertility and Divorce in Sweden
queue.venue: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
queue.note: Swedish essays on partnering, fertility, divorce and HOUSEHOLD FORMATION and dissolution at the individual longitudinal level. Register-grade data covering both links; trace the chapters.

queue.title: Beyond the Nuclear Family: Trends in Children Living in Shared Households
queue.note: Gated decoy. Trends in US children living in SHARED HOUSEHOLDS, SIPP and ACS. The arrangement measured from the child's side; exposure trend.

queue.title: Reconceptualising co-residence in post-growth Japanese society
queue.note: Reconceptualising THREE-GENERATION CO-RESIDENCE in post-growth Japan, noting that pension income and savings made ageing parents financially independent -- so the arrangement's meaning changed even where its prevalence did not. A caution for any trend series that treats co-residence as one construct over time.

queue.title: Families in Asia : a cross-national comparison of household-size and co-residence
queue.venue: LA Referencia (Red Federada de Repositorios Institucionales de Publicaciones Científicas)
queue.note: Household size and CO-RESIDENCE across 12 Asian countries 1980-2010, household and individual perspectives. Companion to the 13-country record in batch 19; keep one at assembly.

queue.title: Adolescents’ Expectations About the Timing of Family Life Events: Unraveling the Role of Value Transmission and Modeling
queue.note: Value transmission versus modelling in the parental home as explanations of adolescents' EXPECTATIONS about the timing of LEAVING HOME and later family events. Intergenerational transmission of the schedule itself -- A.19's mechanism operating on A.23's exposure.

queue.title: Extended living arrangements in Chile: An analysis of subfamilies
queue.note: EXTENDED HOUSEHOLDS in CHILE analysed as SUBFAMILIES -- about a quarter of households 1990-2011, and NOT declining despite other family change. Latin America, and the subfamily unit is the measurement §9 needs for distinguishing a couple within a parental household.

queue.title: Changes in Family Attitudes and Behaviors in East Asia: A Comparative Perspective
queue.note: Comparative East Asian Social Survey modules on family attitudes and formation, Korea, Taiwan and China 2006-2016. Attitude and behaviour trends in the extended arm's region with a harmonised instrument.

queue.title: Millennials and Their Parents: Implications of the New Young Adulthood for Midlife Adults
queue.note: Prolonged youth producing PROLONGED PARENTHOOD, and what that means for midlife parents. The parents'-side framing again; contact and support are the outcomes.

queue.title: Family and household composition in Asia
queue.note: Household composition across 13 ASIAN countries, 1980-2010, census and survey combined, with CO-RESIDENCE WITH PARENTS traced over the life course at the individual level. The best exposure-trend record in the frame for the extended arm's region.

queue.title: Changes in the Order of Family Life Events in 20th-Century Europe: A Cross-Regional Perspective
queue.note: Evolution of the ORDER of four family life events -- LEAVING THE PARENTAL HOME, first cohabitation, first marriage, FIRST PARENTHOOD -- across twentieth-century Europe, using ESS and GGP microdata. The sequencing question at its most direct; §3's problem measured as a changing order rather than assumed.

queue.title: Quick, uncertain, and delayed adults: timing, sequencing and duration of youth-adult transitions in Canada
queue.note: Timing, sequencing and DURATION of youth-adult transitions in a Canadian cohort at 43, with LEAVING HOME as the first-stage marker. Duration is a measure the frame rarely carries.

queue.title: Church Affiliation and Life Course Transitions in The Netherlands, 1850-1970
queue.venue: Social Science Open Access Repository (GESIS – Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences)
queue.note: Church affiliation and life-course transitions across 30,000 reconstructed Dutch life courses 1850-1970. Denomination as a pre-determined driver of the transition sequence; D.1.a seam, historical.

queue.title: El retorno al hogar de los padres en las diferentes etapas de la vida en Francia
queue.note: RETURNING to the parental home in FRANCE at different life stages, including returns after 30, and what motivates leaving versus returning. The boomerang half of link 1, with an older population than the British studies.

queue.title: Early adulthood and family formation
queue.note: Extension of early adulthood in IRELAND and the 'unbundling' of the transition to independent household formation from tightly ordered mid-century sequencing. States the de-sequencing that §3 has to model.

queue.title: Produženi život mladih s roditeljima
queue.note: 'Produzeni zivot mladih s roditeljima' -- the EXTENDED LIVING OF YOUNG PEOPLE WITH PARENTS, its drivers and its consequences, in a Balkan setting. The pre-launch construct as the whole subject; consequences named but not obviously including births.

queue.title: Do Transitions to Adulthood Converge in Europe? An Optimal Matching Analysis of Work–Family Trajectories of Men and Women from 20 European Countries
queue.note: Published version of the 20-country optimal-matching analysis: employment, LEAVING HOME, union formation, marriage and CHILDBEARING as one sequence, men and women over 35, European Social Survey. The sequence approach at the largest scale in the frame.

queue.title: Do We Coreside with Parents and Children Shorter than Before
queue.note: South Korean intergenerational co-residence, arguing it is structured by DEMOGRAPHIC change as well as norms -- mortality decline raises exposure to the 'risk' of co-residence. The availability constraint again, now for a contemporary Asian setting.

queue.title: Inequality in demographic behaviour. How important are parents
queue.note: How far parental social background shapes DEMOGRAPHIC behaviour -- leaving home among the outcomes -- as distinct from socioeconomic outcomes. Link 1's stratification question.

queue.title: Household changes in contemporary China: an analysis based on the four recent censuses
queue.note: Household change across four Chinese censuses 1982-2010: shrinking size, simplifying structure. Exposure trend with census-scale data in the extended arm's key setting.

queue.title: From Emerging to Established
queue.note: Latent class and latent transition analysis of education, LEAVING HOME, work, relationships and PARENTING at ages 20 and 29 in an Australian cohort. The whole sequence in one longitudinal design.

queue.title: Coresidence between Adult Family Members: A Form of Reciprocal Support
queue.note: Co-residence between adult family members as RECIPROCAL SUPPORT, distinguishing an adult child supported by a parent from a parent living in the child's household -- §6's dependency-direction distinction, measured. French Family and Housing survey linked to the 2011 census.

queue.title: Class Inequality and Adult Attainment Projects among Middle-Aged Men in the United States, 1980-2010
queue.note: 'Adult attainment projects' as a bundle of labour force participation, RESIDENTIAL INDEPENDENCE, marriage, PARENTHOOD and homeownership, by class, 1980-2010. Treats the sequence as one object; class gradient is what it estimates.

queue.title: Pathways to Adulthood in Uruguay
queue.note: Sequence analysis of pathways to adulthood in URUGUAY from two national youth surveys. Latin American setting; sequence method.

queue.title: Young Adulthood
queue.note: No abstract; chapter titled 'Young Adulthood'.

queue.title: The Transition to Adulthood Matters
queue.note: No abstract; conference paper 'The Transition to Adulthood Matters'.

queue.title: Relatievormen in Nederland, 1984 ( ORIN )
queue.note: Dutch 1984 cohabitation dataset, including having an INTIMATE RELATIONSHIP WITHOUT LIVING TOGETHER. Data source, and it measures the living-apart-together configuration directly.

queue.title: Gender, Turning Points, and Boomerangs: Returning Home in Young Adulthood in Great Britain
queue.note: Gated anchor. Rates of and factors behind RETURNING to the parental home in Great Britain, against the popular boomerang narrative. Link 1's return half, which §9's ARRANGEMENT_MEASURE has to accommodate.

queue.title: The Effects of the Great Recession on Family Structure and Fertility
queue.venue: The Annals of the American Academy of Political and Social Science
queue.note: Great Recession effects on FAMILY STRUCTURE and fertility together, with fertility down 9-11% and the family activated as an emergency support system. A macro shock moving both links at once; C.5.a owns the treatment.

queue.title: The Capacity of Families to Support Young Australians: Financial Transfers From Parents, Co-Residence and Youth Outcomes
queue.note: No abstract, but the title names the exposure precisely: financial transfers from parents, CO-RESIDENCE and youth outcomes in Australia. Whether a fertility outcome is among them is not visible; trace.

queue.title: Female Migrants and the Transition to Adulthood in Greater Jakarta
queue.venue: The Annals of the American Academy of Political and Social Science
queue.note: Internal MIGRATION and its timing against young women's transition to adulthood in Greater Jakarta. Migration is a way of leaving the parental home that the frame's European records do not capture.

queue.title: Lifestyle and close relationship trends among young adults in Poland
queue.venue: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
queue.note: Relational trends among young Poles, with LIVING ARRANGEMENTS among the behavioural factors reviewed.

queue.title: Transition to Adulthood
queue.note: No abstract; chapter titled 'Transition to Adulthood'.

queue.title: The Life Cycle of Bare Branch Families in China: A Simulation Study
queue.note: Life cycle of Chinese 'bare branch' families, staged as UNMARRIED CO-RESIDENT WITH BOTH PARENTS, then with a surviving parent, then alone. A life-table treatment of permanent pre-launch co-residence caused by the marriage squeeze -- A.10's driver producing A.23's arrangement.

queue.title: Household Size and Structure in Iran: 1976-2006
queue.note: Household size and structure in Iran 1976-2006 alongside a sharp fertility decline. Exposure trend in a setting the frame lacks.

queue.title: The Family Context of Cohabitation and Single Motherhood in Latin America
queue.note: Living arrangements of cohabiting couples and single mothers across Latin American censuses via IPUMS family-interrelationship variables. Exposure trend with micro-data in a thin region.

queue.title: Intergenerational Living Arrangements of Young Married Women in Korea, Japan and China
queue.note: Intergenerational co-residence of YOUNG MARRIED WOMEN across Korea, Japan and China, separating co-residence with natal parents from with parents-in-law -- a distinction §6's configuration split needs and most records collapse. Outcome is the arrangement.

queue.title: Family Change in Europe from a Transition-to-Adulthood Perspective
queue.note: European family change viewed through the transition to adulthood, with DEPARTING THE PARENTAL HOME, partnership formation and having children as the three components. States the chain as a framework.

queue.title: Do Transitions to Adulthood Converge in Europe? An Optimal Matching Analysis of Work-Family Trajectories of Young Adults from 20 European Countries
queue.venue: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
queue.note: Optimal-matching analysis of work-family trajectories in 20 European countries from the European Social Survey, with LEAVING HOME among five sequenced events. Sequence method applied at scale; the convergence question bears on Wall 3.

queue.title: Changes in Family Situations as Reflected in the French Censuses, 1962-2009
queue.note: Fifty years of French census family situations via IPUMS. Exposure trend with a long series and micro-data access.

queue.title: Young Generations, Partnership and Life Stages. Opinions and Attitudes in the Czech Republic
queue.note: Czech young generations' attitudes and the changing transition to adulthood.

queue.title: Reseach on Relation of Family and Living Arrangements of First Generation of Marriaged Only-child
queue.note: Living arrangements of the FIRST GENERATION OF MARRIED ONLY-CHILDREN in China, against non-only-children. A cohort in which the extended-household configuration is structurally forced by the one-child policy -- possible source of exogenous variation in who can co-reside with whom.

queue.title: A life course perspective on social and family formation transitions to adulthood of young men and women in Mexico
queue.note: Mexican transitions to adulthood, splitting SOCIAL transitions (schooling, labour entry, PARENTAL HOME LEAVING) from FAMILY FORMATION transitions. The two links separated by design; Latin American setting.

queue.title: Comparing transitions to motherhood across contexts
queue.note: Comparing transitions to motherhood across contexts, explicitly situating first birth against a PROLONGED transition between youth and adulthood.

queue.title: Nest Leaving in Europe
queue.note: No abstract; 'Nest Leaving in Europe' is squarely link 1 but the outcome is not visible.

queue.title: The changing determinants of UK young adults' living arrangements
queue.note: CHANGING DETERMINANTS of UK young adults' living arrangements, with more now remaining in the parental home despite an early average age at leaving. A within-country trend in the exposure with determinants estimated -- the shape Wall 3 wants, missing only the birth.

queue.title: Being a Good Grandparent: Roles and Expectations in Intergenerational Relationships in Japan and Singapore
queue.note: Grandparent roles in Japan and Singapore against a DECLINE IN THREE-GENERATIONAL HOUSEHOLDS driven by low fertility. Exposure trend, and the reverse arrow is explicit in the framing.

queue.title: Timing and Sequencing of Events Marking the Transition to Adulthood in Two Informal Settlements in Nairobi, Kenya
queue.note: Timing and SEQUENCING of first sex, marriage, BIRTH and INDEPENDENT HOUSING in two Nairobi informal settlements. All four markers in one retrospective survey, in a sub-Saharan setting the frame is thin on.

queue.title: Las mujeres jóvenes y la formación de uniones en España
queue.note: Union formation among young women in SPAIN, against a lengthening stay in the parental home and the rise of PARTNERSHIPS WITHOUT CO-RESIDENCE. The registered setting, and it names the living-apart-together configuration that batch 5 flagged.

queue.title: Livets händelser i glesbygd och tätbygd : En livsbanestudie av ålderskohorten 1968–1971
queue.venue: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
queue.note: Life-course event timing in sparsely populated versus urban Sweden for the 1968-71 cohort, and how timing shapes later residential choice. C.2.g seam.

queue.title: Emptying the Nest: Older Men in the United States, 1880–2000
queue.note: 'Emptying the Nest': the share of married men 60+ living only with their wives rose from 19% to 78% between 1880 and 2000, most of it between 1940 and 1970. The exposure trend measured from the PARENTS' side over 120 years of US census data.

queue.title: Understanding the Impact of Poverty on Critical Events in Emerging Adulthood
queue.note: Poverty and critical events in emerging adulthood; the lengthened transition among vulnerable subgroups.

queue.title: Social Change and the Timing of Family Transitions in West Germany
queue.note: Timing of family transitions in West Germany from GSOEP, testing destandardisation and individualisation. Panel data covering the sequence.

queue.title: Leaving home, rights to support and emancipation
queue.note: Leaving home, rights to support and EMANCIPATION as a legal category. The legal-threshold literature behind design 6; note that this is the sense in which 'emancipation' is used here, which is neither the Spanish residential sense nor the political one.

queue.title: Home is where the heart is: living arrangements of young adults in Brazil. *
queue.note: Living arrangements of young adults in BRAZIL, set against postponement of marriage and fertility. Latin American setting, which the frame is thin on.

queue.title: Working age: safety nets and housing
queue.note: Chapter on the AGE at which young people gain rights to basic income and to housing. That is scope §4 design 1 and design 6 stated as policy architecture; worth reading for which thresholds exist to exploit.

queue.title: Changes in household formation and composition in China since the mid-twentieth century
queue.note: No abstract; changes in household formation and composition in China since the mid-twentieth century. Exposure trend in the extended arm's key setting.

queue.title: Employment Insecurity at Labour Market Entry and Its Impact on Parental Home Leaving and Family Formation
queue.note: EMPLOYMENT INSECURITY at labour market entry against parental home leaving AND family formation, European graduate survey. Both links estimated on one cohort with a plausibly pre-determined exposure; C.5.a owns the treatment, but this is the structure §3 asks for. Priority read.

queue.title: Union formation and fertility in Bulgaria and Russia: a life table description of recent trends
queue.note: Life-table description of union formation and fertility in Bulgaria and Russia from the Generations and Gender Surveys, with LEAVING HOME among the modelled events. Post-socialist settings; the GGS instrument carries both links.

queue.title: Heterogeneity in the Transition to Adulthood: The Cases of Australia, Canada, and the United States
queue.venue: European Journal of Population / Revue européenne de Démographie
queue.note: No abstract; heterogeneity in the transition to adulthood across Australia, Canada and the US. A gated anchor.

queue.title: Changing Transition to Adulthood in Urban Burkina Faso
queue.note: Changing transition to adulthood in urban Burkina Faso from a retrospective cohort survey. Sub-Saharan setting, which the frame is thin on.

queue.title: Generations and Gender Survey (GGS): Towards a Better Understanding of Relationships and Processes in the Life Course
queue.venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
queue.note: Description of the Generations and Gender Survey design and questionnaire. Data source; the GGS is the instrument behind several records in this frame.

queue.title: La transizione allo stato adulto (TSA) di due coorti di giovani italiani
queue.venue: Archivio istituzionale della ricerca (Alma Mater Studiorum Università di Bologna)
queue.note: Two Italian cohorts' transitions to adulthood and their interconnections, from a nationally representative survey. Southern Europe; the interconnection framing is §3's problem.

queue.title: Emerging Youth Transition Patterns in Canada: Opportunities and Risks
queue.note: Emerging youth transition patterns in Canada; policy-facing overview of the delayed transition.

queue.title: "Midlife Crises": Understanding the Changing Nature of Relationships in Middle Age Canadian Families
queue.note: Middle-age transitions in Canadian families, noting that home-leaving by adult children takes longer and that many return. Exposure trend from the parents' side.

queue.title: Less help for mother: The decline in coresidential female support for the mothers of young children, 1880–2000
queue.note: The 1880-2000 decline in CORESIDENTIAL FEMALE SUPPORT available to mothers of young children. This is the extended arm's exposure trend measured over 120 years in the US, and it is the mechanism the grandparental-childcare literature assumes; the outcome here is the availability of help, not fertility.

queue.title: Trends in different family structures, by type of household and stage of the family life cycle
queue.note: Trends in Latin American household structures by family life-cycle stage; exposure trend in a region the frame is thin on.

queue.title: The Transition to Adulthood During the Twentieth Century
queue.note: Century-long overview of the transition to adulthood for 16-30 year olds by sex, nativity and race. Historical context for the exposure trend.

queue.title: Comparison of living arrangements
queue.note: Scottish-English comparison of household and family structure, including the PROPORTION OF YOUNG PEOPLE LIVING WITH PARENTS. Exposure prevalence within one state, which is the within-setting variation Wall 3 asks for.

queue.title: Secondary Schooling and Rural Youth Transitions in Lesotho and Zimbabwe
queue.note: Secondary schooling and rural youth transitions in Lesotho and Zimbabwe, where school attendance makes young people LEAVE HOME SOONER while delaying other adult transitions. Schooling as a driver of the arrangement; C.3.b seam.

queue.title: Work and Family Life Trajectories of Young Canadians: Evidence from the 2001 General Social Survey
queue.note: Work and family life trajectories of young Canadians, framing DELAYED transition to adulthood as investment in career before reproduction -- with parental help named as the enabling resource. Both links present, neither identified.

queue.title: The launch pad: Middle class families and the transition to college

queue.title: Household Formation and Marriage Markets in Rural Areas
queue.note: No abstract; preprint duplicate of the Handbook chapter on household formation and rural marriage markets.

queue.title: Chapter 51 Household Formation and Marriage Markets in Rural Areas
queue.note: No abstract; Handbook of Development Economics chapter on household formation and rural marriage markets. Theory for link 1; duplicate of the RePEc preprint in batch 11.

queue.title: The boomerang age: transitions to adulthood in families
queue.note: 'The Boomerang Age' on less permanent living arrangements among young adults in Western societies. Book review; states the exposure trend.

queue.title: Family reproduction and stem-family system: From Pyrenean valleys to Norwegian farms
queue.note: Comparative study of two stem-family systems, Pyrenean and Norwegian, where the house is continued through non-egalitarian inheritance. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2, and the clearest statement of how a stem system ties household continuity to reproduction.

queue.title: Only Hope
queue.note: Ethnography of China's first one-child generation reaching adulthood, their family relationships and values. Context for the extended arm's largest setting; no estimate.

queue.title: Case studies 3 and 4: the Old Poor Law in England and leaving home in the United States, 1850–1860
queue.note: Case studies of the Old Poor Law in England and LEAVING HOME in the United States 1850-60, as cross-sectional models. Pre-modern, but the Poor Law case is a policy-variation design on the arrangement worth reading for the design-6 enumeration.

queue.title: Family and household in medieval England
queue.note: Family and household in medieval England, with chapters on age at first marriage, family size, LEAVING HOME and servants. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: Introduction: The economic and social aspects of the family life-cycle in traditional and modern Japan
queue.note: Introduction to a symposium on the family life-cycle in traditional and modern Japan, contrasting household size and marriage age with the European pattern. Framing for the extended arm.

queue.title: 'Att blifva sin egen' : ungdomars väg in i vuxenlivet i 1700- och 1800-talens övre Norrland
queue.venue: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
queue.note: Youth transition to adulthood in preindustrial northern Sweden. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: Chance Encounters? Paths to Household Formation in Early Modern England
queue.note: Paths to household formation in early modern England and their role in eighteenth-century population growth. Pre-modern niche; A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: Men, migration, and households in Botswana: an exploration of connections over time and space
queue.note: Argues the residential household is an inadequate and misleading unit in Botswana because domestic groups are not necessarily co-resident. A measurement critique that bears directly on §9's ARRANGEMENT_MEASURE field.

queue.title: Population growth and the family
queue.note: Proto-industrialisation, population growth and family formation. Pre-modern theory; A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: Comparing Family Systems in Europe and Asia: Are There Different Sets of Rules?
queue.note: Comparative household formation rules in Europe and Asia, disputing the joint-East versus single-couple-West dichotomy. Theory for the configuration split, and a Wall 3 caution about cross-national family-system comparisons.

queue.title: [Infant and child mortality, marital fertility, and family economy among peasants in Navarre (1860-1930)].
queue.note: Marital fertility and stem-family household size and composition in rural Navarre 1860-1930, with a dependency ratio computed over co-resident members. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2 but the closest historical analogue of the extended-couple cell.

queue.title: Life Course Perspectives on Women's Autonomy and Health Outcomes
queue.note: Household formation and inheritance patterns as determinants of women's autonomy, contrasting preindustrial northern Europe with contemporary northern India. Theory for the §6 configuration split.

queue.title: Household Forms and Living Standards in Preindustrial France: From Models to Realities
queue.note: Household forms and living standards in preindustrial France; family size and household form over the life course. Pre-modern, A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: A Chinese female postnuptial leaving home model--a procedure for analyzing main parameters alpha and beta in the setting up, testing and estimation of the model.
queue.note: Relational model of post-nuptial home-leaving in China, on Brass-Gompertz lines. Method, not estimate.

queue.title: Effects of changing demographic factors upon women's family status in China: a model of a family status life table and its application.
queue.note: Family-status life table for China with three-generation co-residence as a state; formal, no effect estimate.

queue.title: Le fonctionnement de la famille-souche dans les Baronnies des Pyrénées avant 1914
queue.note: Stem-family functioning in the Pyrenees before 1914, with marital fertility limitation as a Malthusian check. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: Household Formation in Developed Societies
queue.note: Household formation in developed societies as a demand-supply problem, with nine hypotheses for the trend toward separate living. The theory statement for link 1.

queue.title: Hajnal and the Household in Asia: a Comparativist History of the Family in Preindustrial Japan, 1600-1870
queue.note: Hajnal's household formation rules extended to stem-family Japan, relating household formation to fertility. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2 but directly relevant framing.

queue.title: The Demographic Modeling Of Household Cycles: Analytical And Microsimulation Approaches
queue.note: Formal household-cycle demography; fission, fusion and household size.

queue.title: 1. Households: Changing Forms and Functions
queue.note: Anthropological definition of the household as a unit; conceptual, useful for the measurement question in §9.

queue.title: Primogeniture and fertility: fertility models with unequal bequest.
queue.note: Formal fertility models with unequal bequest and primogeniture in pre-industrial England; inheritance rules set who stays. Theory, pre-modern.

queue.title: Fertility and Economic Change in Eighteenth and Nineteenth Century Europe: A Comment
queue.note: Comment on household formation as the route from economic change to English fertility, 18th-19th century. Pre-modern niche; A.7's under Ruling 2.

queue.title: Two Kinds of Preindustrial Household Formation System
queue.note: Hajnal's simple-versus-joint household formation systems. The canonical statement of the pre-modern niche rule; A.7's under Ruling 2, carried here as theory.

queue.title: Fertility, Economy, and Household Formation in England over Three Centuries
queue.note: Household formation rules and fertility in pre-transition England over three centuries. Exactly the pre-modern niche mechanism, which Ruling 2 leaves with A.7; carried here as theory and cross-reference.

queue.title: The Origins of the fertility transition in rural Japan
queue.note: Model of the peasant household under stem-family institutional rules explaining the onset of Japan's fertility transition. Arrangement rules are the exposure but the paper is a model, and the period is FDT rather than SDT.

queue.title: Family type and fertility: a review of literature.
queue.note: REVIEW of the family-type-and-fertility literature, concluding the extended-family-raises-fertility belief is unsupported. Channel 1 was scored as dry; this is the closest thing to a prior review on the extended-household cell and should be read in full.

queue.title: Domestic Development Cycles as a Link between Population Processes and Other Social Processes
queue.note: Stem-family domestic development cycles as a link between demographic and social processes; conceptual.

queue.title: Structural Variability in Stem Family Development Cycles: A Simulation Approach
queue.note: Simulation of stem-family development cycles; residence rules vary, outcome is household composition.

queue.title: Extended Family Structure and Fertility: Some Conceptual and Methodological Issues
queue.venue: Journal of Marriage and the Family
queue.note: Conceptual and methodological critique of the extended-family-raises-fertility proposition, and explicitly notes the scarcity of evidence. Directly on this chapter's cell as framing, no estimate.

queue.title: Some demographic determinants of average household size: An analytic approach
queue.note: Analytic model of how mortality, fertility and marriage age determine household size under nuclear, extended and stem systems. Runs the arrow the other way.

queue.title: Status Transfer of the Household Head in the Stem Family System
queue.note: Stem-family headship transfer in rural Japan; the arrangement is the subject but there is no fertility outcome.
